# Copilot instructions for ScreenForge

ScreenForge is an open-source macOS screen recorder and editor in Rust (egui + wgpu + ffmpeg),
that saves `.screenforge` project packages and imports `.screenstudio` ones. Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and
`docs/STATUS.md` before proposing changes.

## Pull requests
- Title in the imperative, under 70 characters, describing the user-visible effect
  ("Zoom while typing extends automatic zooms"), not the implementation.
- Body: what changed and why, how it was verified (screenshots for UI, `cargo test --workspace`),
  and any follow-up. No AI attribution lines ("Co-Authored-By", "Generated with").
- Apply exactly one category label so the release notes group it: `enhancement`, `bug`,
  `recording`, `export`, `editor`, `ui`, `documentation`, `site`, `dependencies` or
  `breaking change`. Use `skip-changelog` for chores that users should not see.

## Release notes
- Generated by GitHub from merged PRs using `.github/release.yml`; when asked to write or polish
  notes, keep them user-facing: one line per change, start with the feature area, say what the
  user can now do or what no longer breaks. Group under the same headings as `release.yml`.
- Mention required user actions explicitly (new permissions, re-activation, changed defaults).
- Do not list internal refactors, CI or formatting changes unless they affect users.
- Versioning: semantic. Patch for fixes, minor for features, major only for breaking changes to
  project files or the CLI.

## Code conventions
- Rust 2021, `cargo fmt`, no `unwrap()` in UI code paths, errors through `anyhow`/`thiserror`.
- UI: colours from `theme::p()`, icons from `widgets::Icon`, toolbar buttons with 2 px corners,
  text buttons via `widgets::accent_button` / `secondary_button` (see `CLAUDE.md`).
- Project file compatibility is a hard requirement: never change how `.screenforge` files are
  written, or how `.screenstudio` files are imported, without updating the round-trip and import
  tests in `sf-project`.
